title: The Twilight Zone
sub: A blue so faint your eyes invent it
blurb: Between 200 and 1,000 metres there is just enough light to know which way is up, and not enough for anything to grow. It is the largest habitat on the planet, and it holds more fish than the whole of the rest of the ocean put together.
stats: more than all the rest combined

title: Marine Snow
sub: It has been snowing here for ever
blurb: A constant drift of dead plankton, faeces and the shed parts of everything living above. It takes weeks to fall a kilometre, it feeds the entire deep sea, and it carries billions of tonnes of carbon out of the air and down into the floor every year.
stats: the remains of the sunlit zone

title: Most Life Here Glows
blurb: Surveys of the open ocean find that roughly three quarters of the animals make their own light. On land bioluminescence is a curiosity; in the sea it is the commonest way to be alive, used for hunting, hiding, warning and finding a mate.

title: Counter-Illumination
sub: The best place to hide is inside the light
blurb: Seen from below, anything solid is a silhouette against the faint glow from the surface. So lanternfish and many squid light their own bellies to exactly the brightness of the water above them, and erase their own outline.

title: The Biggest Migration on Earth
sub: And it happens every single night
blurb: At dusk, billions of tonnes of animals climb hundreds of metres to feed in the dark, and sink again before dawn. Ships first found it as a false bottom on their sonar — a seabed that rose every evening and fell every morning.

title: The Giant Squid Eye
sub: The largest eye in the animal kingdom
blurb: About 27 centimetres across — the size of a dinner plate, and ten times the width of a human eye. It is almost certainly built to catch one thing: the faint glow stirred up by a sperm whale coming to eat it.
